insight: The hydration break statistics for the Netherlands in the 2026 World Cup reveal some interesting trends in how the team performs after these breaks. Overall, the team tends to gain momentum after a hydration break, with a slight increase in performance in 4 out of 8 breaks, indicating that these pauses may be helping them refocus and come back stronger. Notably, when the Netherlands is not pressing before a hydration break, they tend to perform better afterwards, with an average increase in performance of +0.050 minutes, suggesting that the break gives them a chance to regroup and launch a more effective attack. In contrast, when they are pressing before a break, their performance remains relatively flat, indicating that the break may not be as beneficial in these situations, with the team only managing to maintain momentum half of the time.
